summary: Mirror a binary tree by swapping the left and right children of every node.
mainInsight: Inverting a tree is the same local operation applied to every node: swap its two children. Any traversal (DFS recursion, BFS queue, explicit stack) that visits every node once does it.

approaches.name: Iterative BFS with a queue
approaches.summary: Pop a node, swap its children, enqueue them.
weaknesses: O(n/2) queue for the bottom level

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; recursion is the shortest to write.

promptVariants: What is the core operation of Invert Binary Tree?
options: Swap left and right children at every node (any full traversal)
Reverse the inorder sequence of node values and rebuild the tree
Sort the children of every node by value before recursing
Rotate the whole tree once around its root node pointer
cards.answer: Swap left and right children at every node (any full traversal)
cards.explanation: The mirrored tree is exactly the tree with every node's children exchanged, and order of visiting does not matter.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Reverse the inorder sequence of node val: That describes the effect on values but not how to restructure the tree.

promptVariants: Why does the order of traversal not matter for inversion?
Why is a single pass enough?
cards.answer: The swap at a node is independent of the swaps at other nodes: each node's children are exchanged exactly once, and the children subtrees are inverted by the same rule wherever and whenever they are visited. So any complete traversal (pre-, post-order or BFS) gives the same result.

promptVariants: Compare the space of BFS (queue) and DFS (recursion/stack).
What dominates the memory in your BFS solution?
cards.answer: BFS holds up to one level in the queue: O(w), which can be about n/2 for a complete tree. DFS holds one root-to-leaf path: O(h), which is O(log n) for a balanced tree but O(n) for a skewed one.
cards.explanation: Choose by tree shape if memory matters.

promptVariants: Why is it safe to swap first and then enqueue `current.left` and `current.right`?
What would change if you enqueued before swapping?
cards.answer: After the swap both children are still the same subtrees (just exchanged), so enqueuing either order visits both exactly once. Enqueuing before swapping also works as long as both children are enqueued; only the order of visiting changes.
cards.explanation: The tuple assignment swaps without a temp variable.

promptVariants: What does the function return for an empty tree?
How is a single node handled?
options: None for an empty tree; a single node is unchanged
An error, since there is no node to invert
A new empty node object replacing the tree
The root node with its value swapped to zero
cards.answer: None for an empty tree; a single node is unchanged
cards.explanation: The null check returns None and a leaf swaps two null children (a no-op).

incorrectOptionExplanations.The root node with its value swapped to: Values are never swapped, only children.
